thread.title: The Earnings Beat: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (HD, CSCO, WMT, DE)

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: The Earnings Beat: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (HD, CSCO, WMT, DE)
text:
Shutterstock photo Thanks to a resurgence in oil prices, which closed above $70 per barrel, equities booked another solid week of solid gains. But can it continue, particularly with the oil prices now at four-year highs ?
Led by energy stocks, the Dow Jones industrial average added 91 points on Friday to extend a seven-day winning streak, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq composite added respective gains of 2.4% and 2.7%. The blue-chip index, which has struggled for most of 2018, is now positive for the year.
Sparks from energy giants Exxon Mobil ( XOM ) and Chevron ( CVX ) weren’t the only reason for the Dow’s resurgence. The index also benefited from Apple ( AAPL ), which surged to all-time highs after Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.A , BRK.B ) disclosed a larger stake in the company.
Overall, though, it’s been positive Q1 earnings from banks and techs that has enticed investors back into equities. This week, retailers like JCPenny ( JCP ), Macy’s ( M ) and Dick’s Sporting Goods ( DKS ) will report their numbers, attempting to keep this market rally going. While it’s too early to predict whether they can, here are four stocks to keep an eye on.
Home Depot ( HD ) - Reports before the open, Tuesday, May 15
Wall Street expects Home Depot to earn $2.06 per share on revenue of $25.21 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $1.67 per share on revenue of $23.89 billion.
What to Watch: The housing market has shown no signs of slowing down, and that’s a good thing for the Atlanta-based company, which continues to grow where other retailers have failed. On Tuesday Wall Street will look to see if the Home Depot’s improved merchandising, combined with its online strategy can lead to higher same-store sales, which hast been buoyed over the past year, driven by the fact that consumers spending more money on home-improvement projects while homebuilders are buying more material to build homes.
Cisco ( CSCO ) - Reports after the close, Wednesday, May 16
Wall Street expects Cisco to earn 65 cents per share on revenue of $12.43 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came came to 60 cents per share on revenue of $11.94 billion.
What to Watch: The world’s largest maker of network equipment is working to develop a growth businesses, while managing the mature switching and routing business. Aside from Internet-of-Things, growth areas such as security, the cloud, data center and analytics remain massive opportunities for the company. On Wednesday Wall Street will want to see whether the earnings results and guidance that spooked investors in fiscal Q3 were an overreaction or a sign of things to come.
Walmart ( WMT ) - Reports before the open, Thursday, May 17
Wall Street expects Walmart to earn $1.12 per share on revenue of $120.47 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came came to $1.00 per share on revenue of $117.54 billion.
What to Watch: Shares of Walmart have been under heavy selling, falling as much as 25% from its 52-week high, following the company’s fourth quarter results in February which not only missed on the bottom line (operating income dropped by a significant 7%), but also showed that its online business may be no match for Amazon ( AMZN ) as once perceived. On Thursday the company, despite guiding for weak fiscal 2018 profits, must outline the strength of its e-commerce business and ways to get margins growing again.
Deere ( DE ) - Reports after the close, Friday, May 18
Wall Street expects Deere to earn $3.30 per share on revenue of $9.83 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came came to $2.49 per share on revenue of $7.26 billion.
What to Watch: Global GDP is on a healthy growth pace and accelerating, according to most economists. And these trends, particularly in the United States which is poised to reach 3% GDP growth in 2018, bode well for agricultural equipment and construction specialist John Deere. On Friday, analysts expect John Deere to report strong numbers, driven by a strong housing market and accelerated construction spending.
